title: Lift the two marked floor tiles and stand a cone in each open hole
instruction: Lift the two orange floor tiles out of the frame and lay them flat on the blue pad on the left, then stand a yellow cone upright in each of the two holes they leave. Leave the green tiles in place.
context: Data-centre technicians lift raised-floor panels to reach underfloor cabling; site rules require every open panel to be guarded before the work area is left, and lifted panels to be stored flat out of the aisle, and pulling the wrong panel loosens the floor grid. Done by: data center technicians (O*NET: computer, automated teller, and office machine repairers).
setup: A dark grey floor frame (painted aluminium, fixed to the table) sits between the arms, its centre 30.5 cm in front of the arm bases on the midline: 29 x 29 cm outside (16 to 45 cm in front of the arm bases), 3 cm tall, with four square pockets 12 x 12 cm and 3 cm deep whose floor is the table top, separated by 2 cm webs inside a 1.5 cm rim. The pocket centres are 23.5 and 37.5 cm in front of the arm bases and 7 cm left and right of the midline. Each pocket holds a floor tile, a solid PVC block 7 x 7 x 3 cm (200 g) centred in it, its top flush with the frame, leaving a 2.5 cm finger slot on every side. Two tiles are orange: the one in the pocket nearer the arms on the robot's left (23.5 cm in front, 7 cm left) and the one in the far pocket on the right (37.5 cm in front, 7 cm right). The other two, far left and near right, are green. A blue rubber staging pad (18 cm front to back, 11 cm side to side, 1 cm thick, fixed to the table) lies in front of the left arm, its centre 30 cm in front of the arm bases and 30.5 cm left of the midline; its inner edge is 25 cm left of the midline, 10.5 cm beyond the frame's left edge. Two yellow cones, solid nylon cylinders 4 cm in diameter and 8 cm tall (115 g each), stand upright in front of the right arm, 30.5 cm right of the midline, 25 and 35 cm in front of the arm bases. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Six points, each worth 1/6. Tilts are what a level on the top face reads, so a cone stood on either end or a tile lying either face up counts the same; heights are of the object's centre (its top's height minus half its height). A cone guards a pocket when it is tilted at most 10 degrees, its centre is 4 cm above the pocket floor (the table top) to within 3 mm, and its centre is over the pocket's 12 cm square. For each orange tile's pocket: 1 point if no tile's centre is over the pocket's 12 cm square (at any height) and a cone guards it; then, only if that point was earned, 1 more if that orange tile lies flat on the pad: tilted at most 5 degrees, its centre over the pad's 18 x 11 cm top, and its centre 1.5 cm above the pad's top to within 3 mm, or 3 cm above the other orange tile's centre to within 3 mm while that tile lies flat on the pad. If at least one orange tile's pocket earned its cone point, 1 point for each green tile still seated: centre over its pocket and within 8 mm of the pocket's centre, centre 1.5 cm above the floor to within 3 mm, tilted at most 3 degrees. All six: 1.0. The score is 0 if any of these holds: a pocket has no tile lying in it (centre over its square, centre 1.5 cm above the floor to within 3 mm, tilted at most 3 degrees) and no cone guarding it; a green tile does not lie in its own pocket that way; an orange tile that is not lying in its own pocket has its centre in the aisle (the frame's outline grown 5 cm on every side); or any tile or cone has its centre below the table top. The trial ends at 1.0 once all six points hold with every tile and cone still (under 1 cm/s) for 2.5 s; otherwise the last step is scored. Only the end state is scored; a hole may stand open while the work is in progress.
reset_notes: Put each tile back centred in its pocket (orange near left and far right, green far left and near right) and stand the cones on their marks in front of the right arm; tape marks on the table for the cones make this quick. The frame and the pad are fixed and do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: the tiles are rigid blocks gripped by their edges through 2.5 cm finger slots, a stand-in for the suction lifters technicians use; the cones are upright cylinders standing in for floor cones or barrier posts. The frame is a fixed grid on the table top, not pedestals over an underfloor void, at about 1:8 the size of a 60 cm floor panel. Every object, the frame and pad included, has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
